claims.claim: Auto Loader tracks files in RocksDB in the checkpoint for exactly-once processing; _metadata.file_path is available; checkpoints can live in Volumes paths.

addNewColumns is the default schema evolution mode when no schema is provided; the stream stops with UnknownFieldException and picks up new columns on restart; _rescued_data is added when the schema is inferred.
DataStreamWriter.trigger accepts availableNow=True and toTable exists in PySpark 4.0.
claims.source: Checked on PySpark 4.0.4 in this repository.

concept_html:
Suppliers drop files into a landing folder. You want each file loaded into bronze exactly once, whenever it arrives, without keeping your own list of processed files. Auto Loader does this on Databricks. It is a Structured Streaming source called cloudFiles.

(
    spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
    .option("cloudFiles.format", "csv")
    .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", schema_path)
    .option("header", "true")
    .load(landing_path)
    .select("*", F.col("_metadata.file_path").alias("source_file"))
    .writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path)
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .toTable("research_prod.research_bronze.nat_raw")
)

What each piece does:

  • Checkpoint location. Auto Loader records every discovered file in a key-value store (RocksDB) under the checkpoint. After a failure it resumes where it stopped, and each file path is processed once. One checkpoint per stream, never shared, never deleted casually: deleting it reloads every file.
  • Schema location. Auto Loader infers the schema once, stores it there, and tracks changes. Without a schema you provide, the default mode is addNewColumns: when a new column appears, the stream stops with UnknownFieldException after recording the new schema, and the next start includes the column. Run it from a job that retries, so the restart is automatic.
  • Rescued data. When Auto Loader infers the schema, it adds a _rescued_data column that captures values that do not fit, such as a type mismatch. Count non-null _rescued_data in your contract checks.
  • trigger(availableNow=True) processes every file that has arrived, then stops. Schedule it as a batch job: incremental logic, batch cost.
  • _metadata.file_path gives each row its source file, for the bronze audit columns.

Keep checkpoints and schemas in a Unity Catalog volume, such as /Volumes/research_prod/research_bronze/checkpoints/nat_raw.

lines: def start_bronze_ingest(spark: SparkSession, landing: str, table: str, checkpoint: str, schema_path: str) -> StreamingQuery:
"""Load every new file in landing into bronze once, then stop."""
raw = (
spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
.option("cloudFiles.format", "csv")
.option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", schema_path)
.option("header", "true")
.load(landing)
)
audited = raw.select(
"*",
F.col("_metadata.file_path").alias("source_file"),
F.current_timestamp().alias("ingestion_timestamp"),
)
return (
audited.writeStream.option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
.trigger(availableNow=True)
.toTable(table)
)

title: Auto Loader for file ingestion into bronze
why_html:
A bronze notebook lists the landing folder, compares file names with a hand-maintained "processed.txt", and loads the rest. A timeout kills the notebook after it has loaded a file but before it has updated the list. The next run loads the same file again. Bronze now holds the delivery twice with two ingestion IDs, and silver's newest-version logic cannot tell them apart, because both carry the same delivery_version.

Auto Loader's checkpoint records files and commits the Delta write together, so a restart after a failure neither skips nor repeats a file.
